Buyer Added Bid Specific Scope Of Work(SOW) Text Clause(s) SCOPE OF WORK 1.0 Replacement of HP heater 5A,6A in unit#1 and HP heater 5B in Unit#2 in NNT PS. 2.0 The works listed in the scope for are only indicative and not exhaustive. The e ntire work is to be carried out under the guidance of the NLCIL engineers. The n orms prescribed by the NLCIL engineers are to be kept up. 3.0 Removal of thermal insulation & cladding. 4.0 Providing Suitable temporary arresting supports to feed water Inlet & Outlet pi ping, extraction, drain condensate and other connected lines to prevent free m ovement of the piping during cutting of the piping. The supports to be anchored to the ground if required. 5.0 Cutting of feed water inlet & outlet piping (T1 & T2): [OD:368mm & thickness: 48mm] 6.0 Cutting of steam inlet (extraction) line(S1). 1mm]. 8.0 Cutting the shell side cascading condensate pipes (S2). [Reducer OD :219.1x8. 18/OD 168.3mm & thickness:7.11mm and pipe OD:168.3mm & thickness:7.11m m]. 9.0 Removal of safety valve, level column & other accessories. 10.0 Cutting of pressure & temperature tapping's. 11.0 Dummies if any required for HP Heater piping, same to be fabricated. 12.0 Cutting of start-up vent, shell vent, water side vent and all associated drains of HP Heater. 13.0 Removal of HPH Front side bottom support foundation bolts & shifting of existi ng HP Heater placing at Unloading Bay by using EOT crane. 14.0 Lifting and shifting of new HP heater from unloading bay at "O" ML to HPH posi tion. 15.0 Position the New HPH and fix the front side foundation bolts. 16.0 Prepare edges after removal of dummies for shell & water side (4 Nos) for root welding using TIG. 17.0 Similarly prepare edges of all connecting pipes as per WPS. 18.0 If required, introduce spool piece after cutting the piping to the required lengt h. 19.0 Installation & fixing of Heater. 20.0 Welding of joints using suitable filler/Electrodes. (70S/90S-B3 filler for TIG & 90 18-B3, 7018 and 7018-1 for SMAW). 21.0 Pre-heating & Stress relieving of welding joints followed by Radiography testin g to be carried out as per EWS provided. 22.0 Vendor has to arrange necessary IBR welders for completion work. 23.0 The contractor should engage radiography testing works and the person who i s conducting radiography test must be a Level-II Certificate holder. 23.1 Arrangement of RT Agencies to site to carry out the RT on completion of welding works (preferably in night shifts). 23.2 Mobilisation of Required strength of RT source, film, chemicals for proce ssing, tools & tackles to site and taken back after completion of work. 23.3 Ensure safety against radiation during testing, providing barricade tap a round the working area and restrict movement of un-authorised persons. 23.4 Submission of evaluation reports & Radiographic films of weld joints aft er completion of testing as necessary rectification work has to be carried out if required based on the report. 23.5 For RT machine-should have certification from the appropriate agency with current validity. 24.0 Contractor has to obtain IBR approval from the DOB before the commencemen t of the work. 25.0 All the consumables like cutting wheel, TIG filler wires, electrodes etc shall be arranged by contractor. 26.0 Thermal insulation of the welded portion of all connected lines and new HPH-6 A with supply of LRB wool and other insulation material. Cladding of the newly i nsulated lines portion and HPH shell to be done after completion of the job with supply of aluminium sheet. 27.0 Insulation schedule is attached 28.0 The material must be delivered with the relevant Material test certificate. The test certificate must mention the reference standards and the values (design an d test). 28.1 Lightly resin bonded mineral wool mattresses of density 150 Kg/M3 will be applied for all layers of insulation where hot face temperature is more than 400oC.

28.2 Lightly resin bonded mineral wool mattresses of density 100 Kg/M3 will be applied for all layers of insulation for hot face temp. 400oC and below. 29.0 Housekeeping of the area. 30.0 Scraps & insulation material removed should be shifted and to be dumped in NNTPS scrap yard. ***** THERMAL INSULATION SCHEDULE FOR EQUIPMENTS Design Parameters Cold Face Temp.(°C): 60 Ambient Temp.(°C): 45 Emissivity (Dimensionless): 0.2 Wind velocity (m/sec.): 0.5 Insulation Material: LRB Mattress Material Density: 100 Kg/Cub. Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses SPECIAL CONDITIONS Part-I 1.0 Special grade/ grade 1 boiler license or Heat exchanger repair license issued by Director of Boilers of any state in India should be kept valid throughout the contract period for replacement of HPH-5A and 6A at unit#1 and HPH-5B at unit#2 in NNTPS. 2.0 The contractor should employ qualified supervisor to supervise the work and take care of workman safety and equipment safety and no work shall be carried out without supervisor. 3.0 The contractor must arrange requisite workmen and IBR certified HP welders who have previous ex perience in similar works and must make necessary arrangements to carry out the work in all the thr ee shifts. The contractor should engage IBR certified welders for all the welding works. The welder sh ould possess certificate for carbon/ alloy steel welding on pipelines issued by Chief Inspector of Boile rs of Tamil Nadu, with current validity 4.0 Necessary welding machines, cutting sets, grinding machines, tools & tackles etc in sufficient no's f or execution of work shall be brought by contractor. 5.0 The contractor is solely responsible for any damage caused to any equipment due to improper exec ution of work. The cost of such rectifications will be to his account. The rate quoted shall be firm for t he entire duration of contract and nothing extra shall be payable on any account. 6.0 All safety precautions during cutting and welding to avoid any fire accident shall be strictly adhered to. 7.0 Necessary scaffolding materials for the work shall be brought and erected by contractor. 8.0 Argon, DA, Oxygen required to carry out the job shall be arranged by contractor. 9.0 The contractor shall bring his own safety PPEs & same should be used by his workmen at site. 10.0 The contractor shall abide by the provision of factories act, state factory rules, work men's compens ation act, payment wages act, contractor labour act etc. 11.0 The contractor shall be fully responsible for accidents caused to him or his agents or works men neg ligence or carelessness in regard to the observance of the safety requirements and shall be liable to pay compensation for injuries.

12.0 If any accident/ fire occurs due to negligence of contractor during work, Rs.5000.00/ - will be impos ed as fine. 13.0 The workman engaged must be covered under comprehensive insurance scheme for the particular j ob. 14.0 The work-spot can be any location from 0 to 24 meters height inside NNTPS and the contractor shou ld make their own arrangements to convey the materials to the work- spots for the work. 15.0 When any electrical equipment's are used by the contractor for work, the contractor should engage sufficient qualified and experienced wiremen/electricians. 16.0 Contractor has to continuously engage sufficient number of unskilled/ skilled labourers to execute s mooth work. 17.0 The contractor shall submit the daily labour report to the concerned executive in the beginning of e ach shift. The general shift work should start at 08:30 Hrs and other shifts at 06:00 Hrs ,14:00 Hrs an d 22:00 Hrs sharply. 18.0 Transportation that may be required for men & materials related to the works specified shall be arra nged by the contractor himself. 19.0 The contractor/their workmen and supervisor must have adequate knowledge and awareness of the safety regulations to be adopted while working in NNTPS. Part-II 1.0 SUPERVISOR CHARGES – PENALTY CLAUSE 1.1 In case the specified site supervisor is not engaged by the contractor for the days as per site r equirement, then a penalty of 1.5 times of the supervisory charges shall be deducted fro m the bills of the contractor on pro-rata attendance basis. 1.2 The attendance details of the supervisors shall be maintained with the signature of the super visor, countersigned by the Contractor as well as the NLCIL official concerned. 1.3 Payment of wages to the supervisor and PF and other statutory remittance, if applicable, will b e in the scope of the Contractor. 2.0 Tools & tackles, lifting machines & Safety appliances that are used for the work or by the workmen should posses ISI mark and valid test certificate from the competent authority. 3.0 The Contractor should observe all safety rules and regulations in force and ensure that all necessar y safety precautions are followed up strictly for the safety of workers engaged in the work. 4.0 The Contractor should engage adequate man power having appropriate skills with the approval of t he NLCIL officials to carryout and complete the works. Any extra time / over time engagement of the man power shall be the contractor’s responsibility. 5.0 RATE OF WAGES The present rates of wages payable to various categories of contract workers and Supervisor are as below: TABLE Wages to be paid Categor Dearness allowanc Total wages y Rate of wages e-(DA) w.e.f (Rs. per day) 01.10.2026 (Rs. per day) (Rs. per day) USK 350.00 215 565

SSK / Su pervisor 410.00 251 661 SK 494.00 300 794 HSK 579.00 354 933 6.0 RATE OF WAGES / DA PAYABLE TO THE WORKMEN The contractor has to pay the rates of wages / DA as per Table above as announ ced by NLCIL and any revision of rates of wages / DA from time to time. Howeve r, in case of any revision of rates of wages / DA notified during contract period, t he contractor shall pay the same along with P.F. & ESI component for the variou s categories of labour component. 7.0 RATE REVISION (NOT APPLICABLE). 8.0 CONTRACT WORKMEN DEATH RELIEF FUND (CWDF) 8.1 An amount equivalent to 0.2% (zero point two percent) of gross value of every bill payable (b efore statutory, non statutory deductions) shall be deducted towards “Contract Workmen Deat h Relief Fund” (CWDF) from the contractors for the works carried out by the contractor. No pro vision has been made in the estimate towards the above deduction. 8.2 Based on the modified DRF scheme, monthly contributions to the death relief fund of Contract Workmen / Supervisors shall be deducted by the Contractor Employers concerned @ Rs.25/- fr om every contract workman / Supervisors engaged by Contractor Employer for the works in NL CIL from their salary /wages payable. In order to facilitate this, necessary deduction will be ma de from the bills of the Contractor employers based on Form - D (Attendance Register) & Form -B (Wage Register) Equal monthly contribution to the fund @ Rs.25/- per contract workman / S upervisors will be made by the Principal Employer NLCIL i.e. the Concerned Unit Head / Unit Ac counts Centre. 9.0 CONTRACT WORKMAN AGE The contractor shall not engage workmen beyond 60 years and the Contractor s hall also produce the required age proof for the workmen engaged by him, while applying for entry permit for first time. 10.0 ESI & EPF The Contractor Employers shall be required to undertake the responsibility of re mitting the contribution/ subscription etc., of the contract workman engaged by them towards EPF (EPF & EDLI), ESI etc., (as applicable) and NLCIL as the princip al employer, will ensure compliance under the relevant applicable statutes by ve rifying the remittance made by the Contractor Employers before releasing part / final bills. 11.0 BONUS The contractor shall ensure payment of minimum bonus of 8.33% of the annual

wages to the contract workmen engaged by them for more than 30 days subject to the wages ceiling as provided under Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 and failure i n this regard will be treated as violation of the terms of the contract. 12.0 SAFETY Personal protective equipments (PPE)ie like Helmet, Safety shoe, Goggles etc by to be provided by the contractor and it is in the scope of the contractor. 13.0 PRICE REDUCTION CLAUSE Time is the essence of the contract. In case the contractor fails to complete the works within the stip ulated period (as mentioned in Sl.No.16.2 of Part-II Special Conditions), then, unless such a fa ilure is due to Force Majeure or due to Purchaser’s defaults, the total contract price shall be reduced by ½% (half percent) of the particular job code per day of delay or part thereof subject to a maximu m of 5% of the total contract price, by way of reduction in price for delay and not as penalty. 14.0 GUARANTEE FOR WARRANTY The contractor shall furnish Guarantee for any defective workmanship for a perio d of 6 months from the date of commissioning of HP Heaters (HPH-5A and 6A in unit#1 and HPH-5B in unit#2), in the form of guarantee for warranty (GGW) in a Non - judicial stamp paper of Rs. 100/-. Final payment will be made only on recei pt of the said Guarantee. 15.0 CONTRACT PERFORMANCE GUARANTEE Not Applicable 16.0 PERIOD OF CONTRACT 16.1 Contract Period: 24 months from service start date as per GeM contract. Note: Lead days of 1 day are provided to the Service Provider for necessary mobilization for offering service. Thus the service start date will commence from minimum 1 day after contract genera tion date. 16.2 The period of work is 25 days from the handover of each equipment. 17.0 PAYMENT TERMS 17.1 90 % payment shall be made after completion of the work in all aspects, commissioning, Sub mission of all Radiography reports and acceptance of GGW for each equipment. 17.2 10% Payment shall be made after finalization of contract. 17.3 After receipt and acceptance of the invoice, payment will be released within 30 days. 18.0 GST (Goods and Service Tax) Contractor has to furnish the GST Registration number with relevant docume ntary evidence. Contractor has to comply with the GST Act/ Rules. 19.0 NLCIL reserves the right to short close / extend the contract due to special circumstances. *****
